title: The Burning Oath
premise: Yara Vasquez has spent her whole life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot cross its borders — the only place her runaway apprenticeship could keep her safe. When a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue that only Yara can somehow understand, she learns the child is a living seal binding an ancient entity to the crown of King Aldric, and that the king's regent intends to break it. Fleeing the valley with the child and her estranged mentor's grimoire, Yara joins a ragged company of exiles who become the family she never had. To save them all, she must unbind the king from the thing wearing his crown — a rite that demands she surrender her own memories of everyone she loves. In the end, Yara pays the price, but the found family she made refuses to let her face the forgetting alone, carrying her memories back to her one story at a time.
about_author: R. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and land charters before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people caught in the machinery of old magic, and live somewhere with too many cats and not enough rain.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Years after fleeing her hedge-witch apprenticeship, Yara tends goats in the Hollow, where magic dies at the border stones. A fever-dream of burning crowns haunts her. The chapter establishes her guilt over abandoning her mentor Maren and her fierce, lonely self-sufficiency. Beat: uneasy peace about to shatter.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. During a storm, a mud-caked child appears at her door, mute except for words in a language no living kingdom speaks — words Yara inexplicably understands. The child's eyes reflect flames that aren't there. When Yara touches her, she hears a voice not her own say: 'The oath is breaking.' Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Maren Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara swallows her pride and returns to Maren's cottage, finding her mentor dying of a wasting curse. Maren recognizes the child as a 'seal-child' and gives Yara her grimoire with a warning: the crown remembers what the wearer forgets. She dies at moonset. Beat: grief and inheritance.

chapters.title: Riders on the Border Stones
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Armored riders bearing a crowned-eye sigil reach the valley's edge but cannot cross; their captain offers Yara gold for the child. Yara refuses, realizing the Hollow's protection is now a cage with a siege outside it. The only way out is through. Beat: the point of no return chosen.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara steps past the border stones with the child, Pell, and magic floods back into the world — overwhelming, hungry, and drawn to the child like blood to a shark. Yara discovers she can hear the child's true name: Sefa. Beat: awe and terror of the wider world.

chapters.title: The Company of the Broken Road
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV (fragmented, dreamlike). On the road, they fall in with exiles: Doss, a disgraced knight; Ivetta, a cartographer whose maps show places that don't exist yet; and Brannoc, a gentle giant deserter. Suspicion turns to tentative alliance when Doss recognizes the crowned-eye sigil as the regent Veyra's. Beat: found family begins to assemble.

chapters.title: The Free City of Amberfall
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. The company reaches Amberfall, last free city mustering against Veyra's armies. Its council refuses to believe a child could matter more than fortifications. Ivetta, reading her impossible maps, realizes Veyra's army is marching toward something beneath the mountains — the Oath's original site. Beat: political friction, stakes widen.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Quiet interlude: Yara teaches Sefa common speech while Sefa teaches her fragments of the pre-kingdom language, each word carrying visions of the entity — the Crowned Wound — that was bound long ago. Yara realizes the binding used a person, willingly given. Beat: tenderness deepening the bond, dread underneath.

chapters.title: The Regent's Shadow
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Veyra's assassins strike Amberfall's undercity. Doss, who once served under Veyra, recognizes her methods and confesses he deserted the night she took power. He saves Sefa but is recognized by a surviving assassin, marking the whole company. Beat: loyalty tested, secrets surfaced.

chapters.title: The Council of Ashes
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. Amberfall's council votes to surrender Sefa to Veyra as terms for peace. The company flees by night through Ivetta's unmapped ways, pursued by city guards who were once neighbors. Brannoc holds a gate so the others escape and is captured. Beat: betrayal by institutions, first real loss.

chapters.title: The Grimoire's Price
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Deciphering Maren's grimoire, Yara learns the unbinding rite requires a witness who shares memory with the bound — and that her strange understanding of Sefa's language means she carries a fragment of the original binder's soul. The rite will consume every memory she has of those she loves. Beat: the cost revealed.

chapters.title: Veyra's Offer
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Captured scouts deliver Veyra's message: give up the child and live richly; refuse and watch the free cities burn one by one. Doss argues they should run beyond the sea. Yara refuses — running is how she got here, and it cost her Maren. Beat: the theme crystallizes — loyalty vs. truth vs. survival.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountains
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. Guided by Ivetta's maps of places-that-don't-exist-yet, the company enters the caverns where the first oath was sworn, finding a pre-kingdom hall of standing kings turned to stone mid-kneel. Sefa begins speaking fluently, no longer needing translation. Beat: descent into the story's mythic heart.

chapters.title: The First Binder's Confession
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the stone hall, Yara's inherited memories surface fully: the first binder was a hedge-witch who gave herself to seal the Crowned Wound, and every seal-child since has been her echo. Sefa isn't just a vessel — she's the latest in a line, and the binding is failing because the line wants to end. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Pass
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV (rescued by Doss mid-chapter). Veyra's vanguard reaches the mountain pass above the caverns. The company and a remnant of Amberfall loyalists make a desperate stand. Brannoc, wounded, chooses to stay behind at the chokepoint. Beat: sacrifice, war arriving at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Deep below, the company finds King Aldric — alive, lucid for moments at a time, begging them to end it before the Wound wears him out entirely. Through Sefa, Aldric tells them Veyra isn't the usurper; the Wound is, whispering through him while Veyra merely serves it believing she serves the realm. Beat: moral complexity — even the enemy is bound.

chapters.title: Veyra's Truth
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Veyra arrives with her guard, and instead of battle, Doss confronts her with what Aldric revealed. Shaken, she admits she heard the crown speak and chose obedience because the alternative was admitting she'd been hollowed for years. She stands aside — but her soldiers do not. Beat: antagonist humanized, final obstacle is not her.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. In the stone hall, with armies clashing overhead, Yara begins the rite as witness. Memories burn away one by one — Maren, the valley, Doss's laugh, Sefa's name — as she speaks the first binder's words. The Wound tears free of Aldric; Sefa, choosing freely this time, takes it into herself and dissolves the binding forever. Beat: triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. Aftermath: Aldric, freed but broken, abdicates rather than rule a kingdom built on his captivity. Veyra surrenders her regency to face judgment. The armies stand down. Ivetta draws a new map — one where the mountain hall is marked simply as a grave. Beat: the world remade, quietly.

chapters.title: A Stranger Among Friends
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara wakes with no memories, surrounded by strangers who weep at the sight of her. She knows none of their names, none of her own history — only a warmth she can't explain. Doss introduces himself as if for the first time and asks if he can try again. Beat: grief and gentleness intertwined.

chapters.title: One Story at a Time
chapters.summary: Rotating POVs. The company refuses to let the forgetting win: Doss retells their road, Ivetta shows her maps, Brannoc — scarred but alive — sings the pass, and fragments of Maren's teaching return as stories told aloud. Slowly, memory returns not as it was, but as something shared and therefore stronger. Beat: found family as the answer to loss.

chapters.title: The New Oath
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the rebuilt border stones of the Hollow — no longer a prison but a home with an open gate — Yara swears a new oath, not of binding but of belonging, with Sefa's echo listening kindly from the stones. She remembers everything that matters, because she chose to be told. Final beat: loyalty and truth reconciled; the family stays.
